title: Etale-local normal form of a smooth morphism
statement:
Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be
smooth at $y'\in Y'$. After
replacing $Y,Y'$ by affine neighbourhoods, there are $d\geq0$ and an
etale morphism

$$
e:Y'\longrightarrow\mathbf A^d_Y
$$

such that $g$ is $e$ followed by the projection
$p_d:\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$ of [def-sbc-affine-space].
(*Stacks Project, Morphisms, [Tag `054L`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/054L) = Lemma
29.37.21.*)

proof.text: Use the affine-local smoothness convention identified in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Here smooth at a point has exactly the meaning of Stacks 01V5, definition-smooth (1): there are affine opens $U_0\subseteq Y'$ and $V\subseteq Y$ with $y'\in U_0$, $g(U_0)\subseteq V$ and a smooth induced ring map $R\to A_0$, where $R=\mathcal O_Y(V)$ and $A_0=\mathcal O_{Y'}(U_0)$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. This definition is local at $y'$ and requires no finite-presentation assumption elsewhere on $Y'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], the point $y'$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A_0$.

source.place: Tag 01V5, definition-smooth; Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space, initial affine reduction

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-locally-standard-smooth] to this smooth ring map and $\mathfrak q$. Obtain $h\in A_0\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $(A_0)_h$ is a standard smooth $R$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], $U=D(h)\subseteq U_0$ contains $y'$, is affine, and $A=\mathcal O_{Y'}(U)$ is canonically $(A_0)_h$, with the restriction map as the localization map. Thus $g(U)\subseteq V$. The induced map $R\to A$ is $R\to A_0\to (A_0)_h\cong A$, since restrictions of the structure sheaf compose; consequently this is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras, not just abstract rings.

source.place: Tag 01V7, lemma-smooth-locally-standard-smooth, proof using Algebra Tag 00TA (lemma-smooth-syntomic); Schemes Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine)

proof.text: Let $\lambda:(A_0)_h\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ be the $R$-algebra isomorphism of Step 2. Compose the standard smooth presentation isomorphism to $(A_0)_h$ with $\lambda$; its inverse is the original inverse composed with $\lambda^{-1}$. If $u$ is the original image of the Jacobian determinant with inverse $v$, then $\lambda(u)\lambda(v)=\lambda(uv)=1$, so its image in $A$ remains a unit. By [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], there are $n\geq c\geq0$, $F_1,\ldots,F_c\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $A\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_c)$ under which $\Delta=\det(\partial F_a/\partial x_b)_{1\leq a,b\leq c}$ is a unit in $A$. The definition displays the transpose matrix, which has the same determinant. Set $d=n-c$ and $P=R[x_{c+1},\ldots,x_n]$. The map $j:P\to A$ sends coefficients to their original images and each remaining variable to its class in $A$.

source.place: Tag 00T6, definition-standard-smooth; Morphisms Tag 054L, presentation and choice of the last n-c coordinates

proof.text: There is an $R$-algebra isomorphism $P[x_1,\ldots,x_c]\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$: it fixes $R$ and every variable; its inverse regards $x_{c+1},\ldots,x_n$ as elements of the coefficient algebra $P$ and the first $c$ variables as polynomial variables over $P$. The two composites fix all generators, hence are identities. Passing to the ideals generated by the same $F_a$ gives a $P$-algebra presentation $A\cong P[x_1,\ldots,x_c]/(F_1,\ldots,F_c)$ for the structure map $j$. For a monomial $r\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{k_i}$ and $b\leq c$, differentiation on either side gives $k_b r x_b^{k_b-1}\prod_{i\ne b}x_i^{k_i}$ when $k_b>0$, and zero when $k_b=0$. The factors indexed by $i>c$ are coefficients in $P$. Additivity gives equality of the derivatives for every $F_a$, so its Jacobian matrix is the original matrix. Its determinant is the unit $\Delta$ of Step 3. This is precisely a square Jacobian presentation [def-exc-jacobian-presentation].

source.place: Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space, regrouping variables over R[x_{c+1},...,x_n]

proof.text: Apply the square-presentation-to-etale direction of [lem-exc-etale-jacobian-presentation] over $P$: $j:P\to A$ is etale of finite presentation. Its hypotheses hold because Step 4 has exactly $c$ variables, $c$ relations and invertible determinant. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], the induced morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ is etale. Identify $U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\mathbf A^d_V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}P$, using the affine-base clause of [def-sbc-affine-space] and relabelling the $d$ remaining variables. This gives the required etale morphism $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_V$.

source.place: Tag 054L, conclusion that the regrouped ring map is etale; Tag 02GI, definition-etale, and Tag 02GJ, lemma-etale-characterize; Algebra Tag 00U9, lemma-etale-standard-smooth

proof.text: The projection $p_d:\mathbf A^d_V\to V$ is induced by the constant inclusion $i:R\to P$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. For every $r\in R$, $j(i(r))$ is the original image of $r$ in $A$, because the presentation and all isomorphisms used were $R$-linear. Hence $j\circ i$ is exactly the ring map of the restriction $g|_U:U\to V$. By the functoriality and uniqueness of spectrum morphisms [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and the identification of the induced ring map with the restricted original morphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square], $p_d\circ e=g|_U$. The affine opens $U,V$ contain the designated points, and $d\geq0$ since $n\geq c$; replacing $Y',Y$ by these opens proves the statement.

source.place: Tag 054L, final factorization; Schemes affine functoriality

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be
smooth at $y'\in Y'$. After
replacing $Y,Y'$ by affine neighbourhoods, there are $d\geq0$ and an
etale morphism

$$
e:Y'\longrightarrow\mathbf A^d_Y
$$

such that $g$ is $e$ followed by the projection
$p_d:\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$ of [def-sbc-affine-space].

proof.text:
Choose affine neighbourhoods $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and
$Y'=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of the specified points, small enough
that $g$ is smooth on the latter. We use the ordinary
commutative-algebra infinitesimal criterion: a finitely presented
formally smooth algebra is smooth
([Stacks, Tag 00TN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00TN)),
and near any prime it has a presentation

$$
C=R[x_1,\ldots,x_N]/(F_1,\ldots,F_c),\qquad
\det\left(\frac{\partial F_a}{\partial x_b}\right)_{a,b\leq c}
\in C^\times.
$$

The latter is the standard-presentation lemma of commutative
algebra ([Tag 00TA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00TA)).
Its algebraic mechanism is to choose a basis of the projective
conormal module, then a nonzero minor of its split injection into
the free module of differentials. Localizing at that minor and
using Nakayama on the finitely generated relation ideal gives the
displayed generators; a localization is incorporated by adjoining
one variable and its inverse relation. These operations replace
the source by an affine open containing the selected point.
This is an application of the ring lifting criterion to the local
lifting condition in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

Put $d=N-c$ and regard the last $d$ variables as base
coordinates: let $P=R[x_{c+1},\ldots,x_N]$. The same presentation
is now a $P$-algebra presentation with $c$ variables and $c$
relations, and its square Jacobian determinant is invertible.
It is exactly a presentation of [def-exc-jacobian-presentation].
For clarity, the lifting assertion for this new base can also be
read directly from the equations. Given a square-zero ideal
$J\subset Q$, a $P$-algebra map $C\to Q/J$ determines
arbitrary lifts $q_b$ of the first $c$ variables. Its errors
$F_a(q)$ lie in $J$. A correction $v\in J^c$ must satisfy

$$
(\partial F_a/\partial x_b)(q)\,v_b=-F_a(q).
$$

There is exactly one solution because the determinant is a unit:
it is a unit modulo a nilpotent ideal and hence a unit in $Q$.
Taylor expansion has no higher correction terms since $J^2=0$.
This constructs the unique lift fixing all the base coordinates.
Successive square-zero quotients treat a general nilpotent ideal.
Consequently [lem-exc-etale-jacobian-presentation] makes
$\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ etale.
By [def-sbc-affine-space], $\operatorname{Spec}P=\mathbf A^d_Y$.
The composite with its projection is induced by the original
ring homomorphism $R\to C$, and is therefore exactly $g$.
This constructs the required factorization.
